proof_summary: Lucas-type binomial congruences pair the two ranges of each sum to show that both sequences vanish modulo \(p\) at every \(p+r\) with \(0\le r<p\); at \(p-1\), \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\) gives the first boundary value \(1\), while divisibility of the central binomial factors leaves only \(k=(p-1)/2\) in the second, giving \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Hence each Hankel matrix is anti-triangular modulo \(p\), and reversing its columns expresses its determinant as the reversal sign \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) times the anti-diagonal product, yielding the two claimed residues.
